model_annotation: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and is shown on a logarithmic scale with major tick labels at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³; the plotted points appear at four increasing co-occurrence values (approximately 5, 30, 300, and 3000). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)”, uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from 37% to 67%, with labeled ticks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 38.2% at the smallest co-occurrence value to ~41.8% at the second point, then to ~43.8% at the third point, and ending near ~43.9% at the largest value (nearly flat between the last two points). FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from ~39.7% to ~43.3%, then ~46.2%, and ending at ~47.6%. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, increasing from ~42.8% to ~44.8%, then ~46.6%, and ending at ~49.4%. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, rising from ~44.3% to ~48.8%, then ~54.0%, and ending at ~56.4%. MEMIT is a purple solid line with polygon markers, increasing from ~43.5% to ~51.0%, then ~52.9%, and ending at ~54.7%. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from ~51.0% to ~57.2%, then ~62.3%, and ending at ~66.1%.
